Part 2 of 2
==================================================
[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.25] (2) In this Section—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.25] (a)“claim for environmental review” means a claim made by the Office for Environmental Protection (“OEP”) under section 38 of the Environment Act 2021(1);

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.25] (b)“the environmental review procedure” means the Part 8 procedure as modified by this Section;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.25] (c)“interested party” means any person (other than the claimant and defendant) who is directly affected by the claim; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.25] (d)“court” means the High Court. ## Who may exercise the powers of the High Court

## 54.26

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.26] (1) Rule 54.1A (excluding paragraph (3)(a) of the rule) applies to a claim for environmental review. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.26] (2) A claim for environmental review shall be assigned to the Planning Court. ## When this Section must be used

## 54.27

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.27] (1) The environmental review procedure must be used where a claim for environmental review is made. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.27] (2) Practice Direction 54E applies to the environmental review procedure. ## Time limit for filing claim form

## 54.28

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.28] (1) The claim form must be filed not later than 6 months from the date by which a response to a decision notice was required under section 36(3) of the Environment Act 2021. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.28] (2) The time limit in paragraph (1) may be extended, but only upon application to the court by the claimant and if the court is satisfied that it is reasonable to do so. ## Claim form

## 54.29

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.29] (1) In addition to the matters set out in rule 8.2 (contents of the claim form) the claimant must also state—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.29] (a)the name of the public authority, the defendant, against whom the claim for environmental review is brought;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.29] (b)the name and address of any person the claimant considers to be an interested party; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.29] (c)any remedy (including any interim remedy) sought by the claimant. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.29] (2) The claim form must be accompanied by the documents required by Practice Direction 54E. ## Service of claim form

## 54.30

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.30] The claim form must be served on—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.30] (a)the defendant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.30] (b)unless the court otherwise directs, any person the claimant considers to be an interested party,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.30] within 7 days after the date of issue. ## Acknowledgment of service

## 54.31

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (1) Any person served with the claim form who wishes to take part in the environmental review must file an acknowledgment of service in the relevant practice form in accordance with the following provisions of this rule. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (2) Any acknowledgment of service must be—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (a)filed not more than 35 days after service of the claim form; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (b)served on—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (i)the claimant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (ii)subject to any direction under rule 54.30(b), any other person named in the claim form,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] as soon as practicable and, in any event, not later than 7 days after it is filed. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (3) The time limits under this rule may not be extended by agreement between the parties. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (4) The acknowledgment of service—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (a)must state the name and address of any person the person filing it considers to be an interested party; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (b)may include or be accompanied by an application for directions. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.31] (5) Rule 10.3(2) does not apply. ## Detailed grounds and evidence

## 54.32

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.32] (1) A defendant and any other person served with the claim form who wishes to contest the claim or support it on additional grounds must file and serve with the acknowledgement of service—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.32] (a)detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.32] (b)any written evidence. ## Failure to file acknowledgment of service

## 54.33

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.33] (1) Where a person served with the claim form has failed to file an acknowledgment of service in accordance with rule 54.31 or to comply with 54.32, they may not take part in the hearing of the claim unless the court allows them to do so and they comply with rule 54.31 or any other direction of the court regarding the filing and service of—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.33] (a)detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.33] (b)any written evidence. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.33] (2) Where that person takes part in the hearing of the environmental review, the court may take their failure to file an acknowledgment of service into account when deciding whether an order as to costs should be made. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.33] (3) Rule 8.4 does not apply. ## Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds

## 54.34

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.34] The court’s permission is required if the claimant seeks to rely on grounds other than those set out in the original claim. ## Other procedural rules

## 54.35

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.35] Rules 54.10 and 54.16 – 54.20 shall apply to the environmental review procedure, except that—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.35] (a)references to “permission to proceed” shall be disregarded; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.35] (b)the reference in rule 54.19 to “the decision to which the claim relates” shall be read as referring to “the matter to which the claim relates.”. (1)
